title: Onion Rings, Breaded, Par Fried, Frozen, Prepared, Heated in Oven

content.title: About
content.content: Onion rings are pieces of onion coated in a seasoned breadcrumb mixture, partially fried by steam and then frozen. They are designed for easy oven preparation: preheat to 200 °C and bake for 12‑15 minutes until golden and crisp. The product retains a crunchy texture and the characteristic aroma of fried onion while containing less fat than traditionally deep‑fried rings.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Onion rings first appeared in the United States in the 1950s as a fast‑food snack.
The par‑fry steam step reduces the amount of oil needed for final oven cooking.
Freezing immediately after steam‑frying preserves much of the vitamin C naturally present in onions.
Various breading options exist, from classic wheat flour to gluten‑free rice flour blends.
Sweet yellow onions are typically used to provide a mild flavor and minimal bitterness.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Onions contain quercetin and sulfur compounds that help combat free radicals and support immune function.

items.title: Cardiovascular support
items.content: Phytochemicals in onion can help lower cholesterol levels and improve vascular health.

items.title: Low fat when baked
items.content: Baking without added oil results in significantly fewer calories compared with deep‑fried rings.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Onion rings retain some fiber, which aids normal digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Onions provide vitamin B6 and folate, important for metabolism and nervous system function.

items.title: Onion allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to onion products, ranging from skin rash to severe symptoms.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Prepared rings often contain added salt in the coating; people monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Gastric irritation
items.content: Onion can aggravate gastritis or acid reflux in sensitive persons.

items.title: Added preservatives
items.content: Some brands include preservatives or flavor enhancers; choose additive‑free versions if you have sensitivities.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Onion rings make a great snack with dips (ketchup, mayo, ranch), can be added to burgers or salads, and are ready to bake, microwave, or grill—just ensure even browning.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep frozen rings in a freezer at –18 °C or lower. Once thawed, cook immediately and do not leave at room temperature for more than 2 hours.
